verdict.line: You lose if you eat a clean E (Apprehend) into full Q-W-R before level 6 without Grit charged; you win by trading only on empowered autos and punishing every Apprehend whiff into a Stridebreaker-powered late game.

brief.thesis: The numbers back an even lane — 50.7% Sett winrate over 1090 games, even lane and solo-kill advantage — because both champions are built around the same resource-gate: Darius needs autos landing between abilities to keep Hemorrhage stacked, and Sett needs Pit Grit charged before a trade pays off. Whoever trades on the other's terms loses the exchange. Sett's structural edge is that his empowered hits scale off max health and his kit gets tankier through Stridebreaker into Black Cleaver, so even trades late become Sett trades.

theirWindow.what: A landed Apprehend chains straight into Q's slow and a true-damage W auto with no way for you to disengage — if you feel the pull land, trade back immediately with your own empowered auto rather than trying to walk away, since he resets to full combo faster than you can kite at these levels.

yourWindow.what: Apprehend only pulls on its outer edge and leaves him with no stick tool for several seconds afterward — close the gap, land Q (Knuckle Down)'s alternating hits to bait his Q, then dump your charged Grit auto or E (Facebreaker) before he can reset.

runes.keystoneWhy: Both listed pages run Conqueror — it converts your prolonged melee trades directly into healing, which is what closes out even fights against a champion who has no answer to sustained damage output.

summoners.why: Flash + Ignite is run in 95.3% of games at 51.7% winrate — Ignite offsets Darius's healing off Conqueror and Grasp-style sustain and secures kills once you land your R (The Show Stopper) slam.

playing.title: Trade only at full Grit
playing.detail: Take Darius's Q edge or E pull damage only when it caps your Pit Grit passive — free damage that doesn't charge your empowered auto just feeds his stacking, so disengage instead of absorbing chip for nothing.

playing.title: Punish every Apprehend whiff
playing.detail: Darius's E only pulls on the outer hitbox — if it misses, he has no stick tool for several seconds. Close immediately and unload Q (Knuckle Down) into your charged Haymaker before he can reset.

playing.title: Track the 5-stack execute threshold
playing.detail: Once Hemorrhage hits 5 stacks, his R (Noxian Guillotine) becomes a lethal true-damage finisher. Back off or commit E (Facebreaker) before level 6 rather than sitting at low health inside his ult range.

playing.title: Use E while he winds up Q
playing.detail: Darius has to commit to Q (Decisive Strike)'s cast to get the slow and bonus edge damage — throw Facebreaker in that window to stun him before the edge hit lands, per the matchup's own engage tell.

playing.title: Position minions for a guaranteed E stun
playing.detail: Facebreaker only stuns if enemies are hit on both sides — walk Darius so a minion wave sits opposite him before you commit, otherwise it only slows.

playing.title: Bank Flash for his E, not his R
playing.detail: Since his ult resets on takedown, surviving the initial Apprehend pull matters more than dodging the follow-up Guillotine — save Flash to escape the grab itself.

playing.title: Force the fight when Stridebreaker completes
playing.detail: Your win rate climbs from item spikes, not levels — once Stridebreaker is up, start initiating trades yourself instead of waiting for him to commit first.

brief.patchCaveat: Build paths, runes, summoners, and all win-rate/sample figures above are measured OP.GG data from real games on the current patch; the mechanical reasoning, timings, and trade patterns are my own tactical read layered on top of that data.
